matches.note: –:276-280 Enlil 'who created teeming humankind', Ea 'who pinched off their clay', Mami 'who fashioned them' šarkū ana amēlūti etgura dabāba / sarrāti u lā kināti išrukūši santakku, 'gave perverse speech to humankind, endowed them forever with lies and untruth'; Q 91:7-10 wa-nafsin wa-mā sawwāhā fa-alhamahā fujūrahā wa-taqwāhā qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā wa-qad khāba man dassāhā. The shapers put the bent into humans at their making; the Babylonian gods give only falsehood, the Quranic shaper both wickedness and god-fearing, and the choice decides.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/ane-quran/13-ane-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The makers of humankind themselves gave it lying speech, or the shaper of the soul inspired it with its wickedness and its piety [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Babylonian Theodicy, stanzas 25-27: society honours murderers; the gods gave humans lies; final plea: The creator gods themselves gave humankind twisted speech, lies and falsehood forever; The sufferer protests his humility: he walked unobtrusively, did not raise his voice, did not hold his head high but looked at the ground; Society extols the powerful murderer and oppresses the powerless innocent: they call the wicked truthful, drive off the truthful, fill the oppressor's treasury and empty the poor man's larder; Humility in public: walking modestly, keeping the voice low, not holding the head (cheek) high; The great gods fashion the black-headed people and make the animals multiply; The sun god is shepherd of the land and father of the black-headed; Petition that the angry personal god and personal goddess turn back and be reconciled with the sufferer; The poem is an alphabetic acrostic (lines or stanzas begin with successive letters); First human shaped from dust, clay or soil.

Only in The sun: the soul's two inspirations and the she-camel of God: Thamud's most wretched one rises; the messenger warns 'God's she-camel and her drinking'; they hamstring her and God crushes them; God proportioned the soul and inspired it with (knowledge of) its wickedness and its piety; who purifies it prospers; God spread out the earth as a carpet, cradle or bed (bisat, mihad, daha, sutihat, tahaha); List of destroyed peoples or hosts (e.g. 'Ad, Thamud, Pharaoh) recalled as warning; A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage; Destruction follows the people's rejection of a messenger.

matches.note: wa-nafsin wa-mā sawwāhā fa-alhamahā fujūrahā wa-taqwāhā, qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā wa-qad khāba man dassāhā ~ hă-lôʾ ʾim têṭîv śeʾēt we-ʾim lōʾ têṭîv la-ppetaḥ ḥaṭṭāʾt rōvēṣ ... we-ʾattāh timšol bô: the soul faces good and sin and must master it; in the Quran God himself inspires both, in Genesis sin crouches outside. cf. rabbinic yeṣer ha-ṭôv / yeṣer ha-raʿ (not a match).
